s.line: Aunt Em had just come out of the house to water the cabbages when she looked up and saw Dorothy running toward her.
s.note: רָצָה here is "running" (feminine present of רָץ). Exactly the same spelling and vowels give רָצָה = "he wanted". הִשְׁקָה (hif'il) = to water plants or give someone a drink; שָׁתָה = to drink. לִקְרָאת = toward, to meet; לִקְרַאת הַחַג = ahead of the holiday.

s.line: folding the little girl in her arms and covering her face with kisses.
s.note: כִּסָּה בִּנְשִׁיקוֹת = "covered with kisses", the same image as in English. כִּסָּה (pi'el) = to cover; מִכְסֶה = a lid, כִּסּוּי = a cover.

w: לְכָל הָרוּחוֹת|in the world|~idiom: lit. to all the winds
s.line: “Where in the world did you come from?”
s.note: לְכָל הָרוּחוֹת ("to all the winds") adds force to a question, like "on earth" or "the heck": אֵיפֹה לְכָל הָרוּחוֹת הָיִיתָ? It is informal but not rude.

w: מֵאֶרֶץ אוֹז|from the Land of Oz
s.line: “From the Land of Oz,” said Dorothy gravely.

s.note: When you speak to someone, the title loses its article: הַדּוֹדָה אֶם = Aunt Em (talking about her), דּוֹדָה אֶם! = "Aunt Em!" (calling her).

s.line: I’m so glad to be at home again!”
s.note: בַּבַּיִת = at home (being there), but הַבַּיְתָה = home (going there): אֲנִי בַּבַּיִת / אֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ הַבַּיְתָה. שׁוּב בַּבַּיִת, "home again", is the chapter title.
